name: alpha-linolenic acid
description: Alpha-linolenic acid (CAS 463-40-1 ), commercially known as ALA, is an essential omega-3 fatty acid sourced primarily from flaxseed, chia, and other plant-based oils. As a bioactive lipid ingredient, it functions as a nutritional supplement component, skin-conditioning agent, and emulsifier across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing. In functional food and dietary supplement production, ALA is incorporated into fortified oils, capsules, and nutritional blends to deliver plant-sourced omega-3 content to finished products. Personal care formulators use it in facial oils, moisturizers, and hair treatments, where its skin-barrier-supporting properties justify premium positioning in naturals-oriented product lines. Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate ALA into softgel and lipid-based drug delivery systems requiring a defined fatty acid profile for specialized therapeutic applications. In specialty emulsion formulations, it contributes to dispersion stability in products where polyunsaturated fatty acid composition is a labeled or regulated specification. Alpha-linolenic acid is supplied as a liquid oil, typically in bulk drums or intermediate bulk containers, and as standardized flaxseed oil fractions with defined ALA content. Food-grade and USP -grade specifications are available to meet regulatory requirements across nutrition and pharmaceutical applications. Technical-grade material is also offered.
